lines: The men dug in the crater for an hour. They found only his identity disc. Edmund Acquillae.
This is Front News. Day four.
For a second night, the guns on Verdel Ridge fired on the Hegemony.
Twenty-six men were hit. Ten were killed where they stood, by direct hits.
The bearers could not reach every stretcher under the shells.
And the shells did something worse. They tore down the wire.
Only a quarter of the Hegemony wire was still standing. In twenty-three sectors, a man could walk straight through.
So the call went out for wiring parties. Crawl out after dark, fix the wire, and when a flare goes up, drop flat and wait.
In the Hegemony hospital, every bed was full. Twenty-three men waited on stretchers.
The medics could reach two out of three.
The Concord did not get away clean. Norbert Fransinlak, a Hegemony sniper, was watching their parapet.
Isidor Jackmdunn looked over it for one second too long.
Day four cost the Hegemony eleven dead. The Concord, three.
Edmund Acquillae's family kept sending men. Today the third Acquillae serves on the line. A medic.
And something new began. Three soldiers bought War Bonds with their own money, to keep the front fed.
Through the rain, eighty-one new soldiers came up the line.
The Hegemony now held one hundred and seventy. The Concord, one hundred and fifty.
In the race for Hill 304, the Hegemony pulled far ahead. Seventy-six to fifty.
Twenty-four more, and the hill is theirs.
This was Front News. Next time: the hill.
